title: Confidence Intervals for Variance and Standard Deviation

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The chi-square distribution is used for confidence intervals for variance and standard deviation.
questions.prompt: Which distribution is used to construct a confidence interval for a population variance or standard deviation?
hints: It is positively skewed and uses degrees of freedom.
Not symmetric like z or t.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Degrees of freedom for a chi-square distribution used for variance is n - 1.
questions.prompt: For a sample of size n, the chi-square distribution has degrees of freedom equal to ___.
hints: It is one less than the sample size.
It is the square of the sample standard deviation.
Denoted by s².
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The point estimate for $\sigma^2$ is the sample variance s².
questions.prompt: What is the point estimate for the population variance $\sigma^2$?
What shape does the chi-square distribution have?
hints: It has a long right tail.
All chi-square values are ≥ 0.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The chi-square distribution is positively skewed.

hints: One is for the left tail, one for the right tail.
There are two: χ²_L and χ²_R.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Two critical values are needed: χ²_L and χ²_R.
questions.prompt: How many critical values are needed to construct a confidence interval for a population variance using the chi-square distribution?

hints: It equals (1 - c)/2.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The area to the right of $\chi^2_R$ is 0.025.
questions.prompt: For a 95% confidence interval for the population variance, the area to the right of $\chi^2_R$ is ___.

hints: The larger critical value goes in the denominator of the lower bound.
Remember: χ²_R > χ²_L.
questions.prompt: The confidence interval for the population variance $\sigma^2$ is given by:
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The correct formula is $\frac{(n-1)s^2}{\chi^2_R} < \sigma^2 < \frac{(n-1)s^2}{\chi^2_L}$.

questions.prompt: How do you obtain a confidence interval for the population standard deviation $\sigma$ from the interval for $\sigma^2$?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Take the square root of each endpoint of the $\sigma^2$ interval.
hints: It undoes the squaring.
You apply the same operation to both endpoints.

questions.prompt: What is the required condition for using the chi-square method to construct a confidence interval for a population variance?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The population must be approximately normally distributed.
hints: The chi-square distribution assumes a specific shape for the population.
This is unlike the z-interval for means, which can rely on large samples.
options: The sample size must be at least 30.
The population must be normally distributed.
The population standard deviation must be known.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The formula is =CHISQ.INV.RT(0.025, 15).
hints: The first argument is the probability in the right tail.

hints: Check if the entire interval is below the limit.

hints: Think about the shape of the chi-square distribution.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The chi-square distribution becomes more symmetric with larger degrees of freedom.
hints: The skewness decreases.
